# share.notambourine.com

Private artifact sharing. Upload a file or folder, get an unguessable branded
URL, hand it to one person. This file is the whole API.

## Auth

Writes need `Authorization: Bearer <token>`: either your raw vault token or a
short-lived session token (see Session). Load the raw token from 1Password by
reference; never paste it into a transcript or a shell history. Convention:
it lives in your Employee vault as item `share-token`, field `credential`.
Run a raw-token command under this prefix (op run resolves the reference from
the environment; single-quote the inner command so your shell does not expand
$SHARE_TOKEN early):

    SHARE_TOKEN=op://Employee/share-token/credential op run -- sh -c '<command>'

Reads need nothing: the unguessable hash in the URL is the credential.
Signed-tier artifacts additionally need a `/k/<token>/` path segment.

## Session

Trade the vault token for a session token once, then run every upload with
the session token and no 1Password unlock:

    curl -sS -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHARE_TOKEN" \
      https://share.notambourine.com/session

Returns 201 {token, name, expiresAt}. ttl defaults to 5m (?ttl=, cap 1h).
Convention: write the response to ~/.cache/notambourine-share/session.json
(mode 0600) and read the token from there per upload, AWS-STS-cache style,
so the token never enters a transcript or shell history.
The session token authorizes /up only: sign, list, and delete still need the
vault token, and a session cannot mint another session, so an exfiltrated
session token caps at a few minutes of uploads. A 401 here means the server
rejects your vault token itself. An expired session 401s with "session
expired" on upload; mint a new one and retry.

## Upload

    curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHARE_TOKEN" \
      -F f=@out/report.html https://share.notambourine.com/up/<space>

Returns the share URL as plain text (`Accept: application/json` for JSON).
Multiple `-F f=@...` fields keep their relative paths, so a folder with an
`index.html` serves as a real page with its own CSS, JS, and images.

Query parameters:
  tier=open|signed   default open; signed requires a minted /k/ token to view
  ttl=<dur>|forever  fixed artifact expiry, default 90d (e.g. 7d, 12h, 4w)
  idle=<dur>         expire this long after last access instead of a fixed date

## Mint a signed link

    curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHARE_TOKEN" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"path":"<space>/<hash>","ttl":"30d","short":true}' \
      https://share.notambourine.com/sign

Returns {url, exp, short?}. ttl defaults to 30d; "forever" never expires.
short:true also mints a /z/<id> shortlink that 302s to the signed URL.

## List a space

    curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHARE_TOKEN" \
      https://share.notambourine.com/<space>/

JSON, newest first. Without the Bearer header this path returns 404.

## Revoke

    curl -sS -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHARE_TOKEN" \
      https://share.notambourine.com/<space>/<hash>/

Soft delete: the upload moves to trash and purges 90 days later. The live
link dies within 10 minutes (cache lifetime).

## Viewing

The same URL renders for browsers and serves raw bytes to everything else
(curl, <img src>, Slack unfurls). Overrides: ?raw forces bytes, ?view forces
the branded shell, ?slides renders markdown as a deck, ?view=source shows
uploaded HTML highlighted instead of executed.

Decks render with Marp. --- splits slides, and Marp directives apply:
<!-- _class: lead --> centers a title slide, <!-- paginate: true --> numbers
them. Arrow keys move between slides and the #n fragment links to one.

## Formats

Append a suffix to a markdown share URL for a branded export. A suffix decides
the output on its own, so Accept gets no vote, and a file uploaded under the
suffixed name always wins over the export.

    deck.md                 branded document, rendered in the browser
    deck.md.slides.html     branded deck, rendered in the browser (same as ?slides)
    deck.md.html            self-contained page: fonts inlined, opens offline
    deck.md.pdf             PDF, deck or document decided from the content
    deck.md.slides.pdf      PDF, always a deck
    deck.md.doc.pdf         PDF, always a document

Bare .pdf and .html read the content to choose: `marp: true` front matter or
`---` slide separators mean deck, anything else means document. Name
.slides.pdf or .doc.pdf when you want to decide instead of guessing.

PDFs render in a headless browser and then cache, so the first request after an
upload can take a few seconds. When the daily browser budget is spent the URL
serves the browser-rendered shell rather than an error.

## Skill

GET /SKILL.md is a drop-in Claude skill covering all five verbs.
